milestone.title: mp-code-review skill — turn docs/code-review-lessons.md into a runnable review agent

intent.outcome: M99's original `mp-code-review` content (the lesson-pattern library as a runnable skill) has been subsumed into the reviewing sub-mode of `mp-coordinator` (M121) per the user's two-agent / four-role architecture. M99 stays as the historical anchor: the canonical home for the lesson-pattern library is now `templates/skills/mp-code-review/SKILL.md` (the procedural wrapper over the patterns); the deep-dive of when/how to run the patterns lives in M121's reviewing sub-mode. The lesson patterns themselves (`docs/code-review-lessons.md`) are unchanged — M99/M121 are split across the content (lessons) vs. the procedure (when to run them). M121 references M99 as the primary sub-skill for the reviewing sub-mode.

problem.description: M99 was the original mp-code-review skill spec. The two-agent / four-role architecture requires the reviewing sub-mode to live inside the coordinator's role skill, not as a top-level separate skill. The mp-code-review SKILL.md stays (as the procedural wrapper over the lesson-pattern library), but the reviewing deep-dive (when to run the patterns, the two-round review discipline, the L5 session-boundary rule) lives in M121's `mp-coordinator/reviewing.md`. M99 is preserved as the historical anchor; the canonical work is in M121. M123 (`mp-handoff`) carries the cross-cutting hand-off protocol between the runner's executing sub-mode and the coordinator's reviewing sub-mode.

in_scope: Author Pattern: blocks in docs/code-review-lessons.md for the chosen lessons (the doc currently has zero Pattern: blocks)
SKILL.md covers the review lifecycle: pre-screen (run pattern checks), read (walk lessons checklist), reproduce (empirical edge cases), file (via mp reviews finding add), re-check (post-remediation)

Pre-screen pattern library mapping >=5 lessons to runnable grep/ripgrep patterns, pinned to exact lesson titles: L6 'New bulk paths that bypass single-path validation', L8 'Operation-level args that re-validate per target', L13 'Dead code sneaking in via refactors', L14 'Awkward control flow left over from earlier iterations', L15 'Tests written against the implementation, not the spec'
Each pattern ships with a positive fixture (must match) and a negative fixture (must not match)
Pre-screen regression suite runs the patterns against the M94 commit range and catches a representative subset (>=3 of F-01..F-10 spanning >=2 distinct lesson categories), not just one
mp install --check (delivered by M98) enforces bidirectional consistency: every Pattern: block has an owner script in the skill and vice versa
Skill embeds or links the lessons catalog so a reviewer without repo access can still run it
Install hook: mp-code-review registers via the skill registry (mp install --skills=mp-code-review, delivered by M98)
out_of_scope: Replacing human review (the skill is a force multiplier, not a replacement)
Auto-fixing findings (the skill files; mp-flow remediates)
Cross-repo review (scoped to mp / repos that follow the same plan-discipline)
Replacing mp reviews pass (mp-code-review calls it; does not replace it)
Building mp install --check or the skill registry itself (owned by M98; M99 consumes them)

acceptance_criteria.description: Pattern: blocks authored in docs/code-review-lessons.md for L6, L8, L13, L14, L15 (the doc starts with zero; each block carries the pattern + a positive and negative fixture)
acceptance_criteria.verification: cargo test -p mp --test code_review_patterns 2>&1 | tail -5; grep -q 'test result: ok'

Pattern library ships >=5 runnable grep/ripgrep patterns pinned to exact lesson titles (L6, L8, L13, L14, L15); each has a positive fixture (must match) and a negative fixture (must not match)
Pre-screen regression suite run against the M94 commit range catches >=3 of F-01..F-10 spanning >=2 distinct lesson categories (not just one easy catch)

design_decisions.choice: docs/code-review-lessons.md is the only editable copy of the patterns catalog. Single source of truth principle. The skill is a build artifact generated from the doc; humans edit the doc via PR, not the skill directly. mp install syncs doc → skill one-way; mp install --check fails the build when a Pattern: block in the doc has no corresponding script in the skill (or vice versa). The procedural deep-dive (when to run the patterns, the two-round review discipline, the L5 session-boundary rule) lives in M121's `mp-coordinator/reviewing.md` — M99 owns the patterns, M121 owns the procedure.
design_decisions.rationale: Single source of truth principle. The skill is a build artifact generated from the doc; humans edit the doc via PR, not the skill directly. mp install syncs doc → skill one-way; mp install --check fails the build when a Pattern: block in the doc has no corresponding script in the skill (or vice versa).

design_decisions.choice: Lessons without a Pattern: block stay doc-only
design_decisions.rationale: Some lessons (methodology, policy, wisdom like L1, L5, L11, L15, L17, L19, L20) don't reduce to runnable grep/lint checks. Forcing them into pattern form would lose the educational layer. The doc captures the why; the skill captures the what-runs. The skill is the runtime slice of the playbook; the doc is the playbook.

design_decisions.choice: L15 is a PATTERN lesson (correcting the earlier design_decision that listed L15 as non-pattern)
design_decisions.rationale: L15 'Tests written against the implementation, not the spec' is runnable: a grep for tests that assert on private/internal module state or that mirror implementation structure rather than spec behavior. The non-pattern set is therefore L1, L5, L11, L17, L19, L20 (methodology/policy/wisdom). Resolves the contradiction between the original scope (L15 as pattern) and the original design_decision #2 (L15 as non-pattern).
